sentences.text: I am applying for the Backend Platform Engineer role at Orion Payments.
At Alpha Pay I worked on the payment approval path, and then on one deployment method that every team shares.
I choose work by asking whether I can cut the path along which one failure spreads to the next service.
Your posting says that when payments stop, money is lost at once. That is why I split the approval path away from the rest of the application, so that a deployment could no longer stop it.
I moved approval out of a single application into its own unit that ships and rolls back alone, and gave every request an idempotency key so that a retry cannot lead to a duplicate approval.

At Beta Commerce I replaced the direct calls from the order service to settlement and alerts with Kafka events, and used the order number as the partition key so that the states of one order keep their sequence.

The deployment scripts that each team had written for itself now live in one Argo CD setup, and the settings of every environment sit in Helm values in a single repository, reviewed before they are applied.
A change goes through review and merge in the repository, lands in staging first so that its state can be checked, and only the approved version is synchronised to production.
Deployment history and rollback share one screen, so what runs in production does not depend on anyone's memory.
For the event pipeline I watched the consumer lag as a metric and set the threshold for alerts.
For order incidents I wrote down a response procedure for each type of failure and used the document to train the people on call.
When something breaks I narrow the cause one layer at a time, and I move repeated operations into automation.
Approval work at Alpha Pay and order events at Beta Commerce give me working knowledge of payment and commerce systems.
Moving from orders to payments was part of the same work: cutting the paths along which failures spread.
I have answered the lines of your posting one by one with work I have done.
I would welcome the chance to talk about it. Thank you for your consideration.

posting.overview: At Orion Payments we run a payment service that connects merchants and shoppers. When payments stop, money is lost at once, so we care most about the stability of the approval path and about how we ship changes. The platform team builds and runs the deployment, observability and incident tools that the payment developers use.
